question.text: On reaction with stronger oxidizing agent like <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>KIO</mi><mn>4</mn></msub></math>, hydrogen peroxide oxidizes with the evolution of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math>. The oxidation number of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi></math> in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>KIO</mi><mn>4</mn></msub></math> changes to

solution.text:
Hydrogen peroxide acts as an oxidising as well as reducing agent in both acidic and alkaline media.

But its reducing action is more effective in alkaline medium

KIO4+H2O2→KIO3+O2+H2O

The oxidation number of iodine in IO3- is +5

The geometry of iodine containing compound changes from tetrahedral to pyramidal in the above reaction
